10.1002_aenm.202503135: For the enhanced energy density and safety of lithium batteries, the development of solid‐state electrolytes (SSEs) compatible with high‐voltage cathode materials has become a primary objective. In this study, a halide‐based solid‐state electrolyte with a Li 3 InCl 6 (LIC) structure is engineered through a dual‐doping strategy, which enables its application with LiCoO 2 (LCO) and LiNi 0.5 Mn 1.5 O 4 (LNMO) cathodes. Fluorine doping is introduced into the LIC SSE to widen its electrochemical stability window. However, this modification leads to a reduction in ionic conductivity. To address this issue, a small amount of Zr 4+ is co‐doped to partially substitute In 3+ , which introduces lithium vacancies that facilitate Li + diffusion and enhance ionic conductivity. The optimized composition, Li 2.9 In 0.9 Zr 0.1 Cl 5.2 F 0.8 (LIZCF), exhibits the best balance of high ionic conductivity (1.37 x 10 −3 S cm −1 ) and a wide electrochemical stability window. When applied in high‐voltage cathode‐based cells, fluorine doping is found to improve cycling stability, while Zr co‐doping effectively reduces the overpotential during operation. Furthermore, partial density of states (PDOS) calculations confirm that the dual‐doping strategy suppresses side reactions. These findings demonstrate the strong potential of the dual‐doping approach for the development of next‐generation high‐energy solid‐state battery systems.
10.1002_anie.8502839: Solar‐driven interfacial photothermal evaporation is a promising approach for desalination; however, its efficiency is often constrained by the narrow absorption range and relatively low photothermal conversion efficiency of existing photothermal materials. Here, we report a large‑anion‐stabilized radical π‐aggregate strategy to construct a stable organic radical‐decatungstate hybrid via mild and controllable electro‑oxidation. The resulting material exhibits full‑spectrum solar absorption with a high solar absorptivity of 95.85% and achieves a photothermal conversion efficiency of 98.24%. When fabricated into a 2D solar steam evaporator, it delivers a net evaporation rate of 1.40 kg·m −2 ·h −1 , approaching the theoretical limit. Further integration into a 3D solar steam evaporator enables long‑term and reliable seawater desalination without salt precipitation. Theoretical calculations reveal that the ultrabroad and intense absorption originates from organic radical π‑aggregates and inorganic polyanion‑synergized intermolecular and intramolecular transfer transitions. This work integrates electrochemical radical generation with the structural advantages of polyoxometalates (POMs) to create a low‐cost, stable, and full‑spectrum photothermal material, opening a new avenue toward efficient and sustainable solar‑driven desalination.
10.1002_smll.202511151: Two redox reactions, V 3+ /V 4+ and V 4+ /V 5+ , are accepted in Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 (NVP) during the charge/discharge process. The discharge capacity at the higher‐voltage plateau ≈4.0 V varies with the heteroatom doping. To clarify this behavior, the V/PO 4 3− ratio is tuned in this work. The results reveal that the composition of 3Na‐0.9V‐3PO 4 is composed of the Na 7 V 4 (P 2 O 7 ) 4 PO 4 (NVPP) phase. Owing to the increased electron density around V donated by citrate ions, the apparent valence state approaches +3, resulting in a poor EPR signal. In the 3Na‐ x V‐3PO 4 /C( x = 0.9–1.5) composites, the proportion of rod/tubular‐like NVPP regularly decreases, while the NVP phase becomes increasingly dominant with rising V content. This evolution is clearly reflected in the CV curves. NVPP/C phase delivers a discharge capacity of ≈40 mAh g −1 at 117 mA g −1 with a voltage plateau near 3.8 V. As the V content increases, this high‐voltage plateau becomes shorter, while that plateau associated with NVP/C extends, leading to the increase in discharge capacity. Crystal structure and the morphology of these composites remain stable, as well as the peak of V 2p 1/2 shifts during charging/discharging, while the electron signal at the V 2p 3/2 orbital nearly disappears. These finding offers a strategy to enhance high‐voltage plateaus in sodium‐ion batteries.
10.1039_d5ta05348j: Mn-doped NiO enables efficient methanol electroreforming into formate, achieving high current density, above 97% faradaic efficiency, and long-term stability, while lowering energy input for hydrogen production and value-added chemical generation than the traditional water splitting.
10.1039_d6ta02911f: Self-assembled multiphase cathodes with exsolved nanoparticles establish extended active interfaces and efficient charge transport, enabling high-performance, durable protonic ceramic fuel cells.
10.1109_tpel.2026.3673572: Fuel cell vehicles have broad prospects in the field of transportation electrification, while their operating characteristics limit their application in complex working conditions. As a result, fuel cell vehicles are generally equipped with Li-ion batteries or ultra-capacitors as auxiliary power sources. An energy management strategy (EMS) is essential to maintain the efficient, stable, and reliable operation of fuel cell hybrid electric vehicles (FCHEVs). In this work, a driving pattern recognition (DPR) method is introduced to improve the adaptability of the EMS. First, fuzzy C-means (FCM) clustering is applied to classify different driving patterns, facilitating the construction of representative driving cycles. Under each driving cycle, the parameters of fuzzy logic controllers are optimized using a genetic algorithm (GA). Finally, the corresponding fuzzy logic controller is invoked based on the DPR results for power allocation in this hybrid power electronic system. The proposed method reduces the overall cost by at least 9.94% compared with a fuzzy logic control strategy, while remaining within 1.83% of the dynamic programming strategy, demonstrating its near-optimal performance with real time feasibility.
